title: Choose Sparton's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Price Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Price Board
options.lineage: split-flap quotation boards of the old exchange hall and the station concourse
options.thesis: Every competitor price is a flap that turns; Sparton is the board that shows what moved since you last looked.
options.viewport: A full-width departure-style board of real-shaped competitor rows (demo data, labelled) whose prices flip in place while the headline and 'Start free' sit above it.
options.risk: Reads as stock-trading if the rows speak in tickers instead of products and shops.

raised.raise: State is a mark, not a hue: exact rows are solid tiles, extracted rows hatched, sold-out struck through.
An attract loop: before signup the landing board cycles a week of demo changes on its own.
Whole-step motion only: flaps turn in whole characters with a step easing, never a smooth tween.
One time axis rules every view: changes, reports and crawls line up on the same weekly ruling.
Your price is a solid line, competitors' dashed, in every price history.

options.label: Shelf Label & Weekly Folder
options.lineage: Dutch supermarket shelf labels and the weekly deals folder
options.thesis: Competitor changes as the shelf labels every shop owner reads: was-price struck through, new price big, the deal flagged.
options.viewport: A folder spread of this week's competitor moves as shelf labels, with the offer and 'Start free' on the cover strip.
options.risk: The most familiar retail look; can read as cheap discounting instead of intelligence.

options.label: Sliding Planes
options.thesis: One room of sliding primary planes: shops, competitors and changes are positions of the same space.
options.viewport: White and grey planes with one red edge that slides to reveal this week's biggest competitor move.
options.case: Strong Dutch identification; loses on clarity because prices and proof aren't native to the form.
options.risk: Becomes De Stijl wallpaper if the planes don't actually move and carry data.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: Changes as frames on a rail, flagged where you stopped.
options.viewport: A perforated rail of this week's changes across an orange field.
options.case: Shop owners don't live at an editing bench, and the rail hides the prices.
options.kept: State as a mark, not a hue.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: Competitors as windows on a dithered desktop.
options.case: Nostalgia for a different audience; prices lose their weight in pixel type.

options.label: Arcade Marquee Row
options.thesis: One cabinet per competitor down a dark aisle.
options.viewport: A dark aisle of glowing competitor marquees.
options.case: Undermines trust in the numbers; wrong register for a pricing tool.

options.label: Deep Dive
options.viewport: A vertical dive profile of the week's changes.
options.case: Beautiful metaphor with no link to shop owners' work.

options.label: Sewing Pattern
options.viewport: A tissue sheet of nested price lines.
options.case: Charming but indirect; owners would decode it before trusting it.
options.kept: Your line solid, the others dashed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS landing page and dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline, product screenshot, three feature blocks, pricing cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other SaaS tool by design.
